objective: Select the next measured workstream after closing the broader filelist shape-sweep public-pack externalization boundary.

decision.reason: The accepted broader shape-sweep evidence proves coverage-output equivalence for the same two reviewed filelist-derived targets at 64x1 and 1x64, but explicitly carries no timing, speedup, repeat-median, GEM comparison, native Verilator option, runtime/ABI, arbitrary RTL, or automatic optimal allocation claim. The conservative next step is single-run timing for the same four target/shape pairs before deciding whether repeat-median timing, resident optimization, native-option work, dependency inference, or policy broadening is justified.

deferred_candidates.reason: A native option boundary is strategically important, but it would shift to integration before the latest broader-shape correctness evidence has any timing basis.
The broader shape sweep is correctness-only. Policy broadening should wait until timing behavior for the same shapes is at least measured once and preferably repeat-median reviewed.
The accepted filelist flows still rely on explicit complete source closure or known-template copied closure. Arbitrary dependency inference is a separate non-claim.
Resident/runtime work may become the right mitigation if 1x64 timing confirms repeated-step weakness, but it should follow the broader-shape timing measurement rather than precede it.
Repeat-median is likely the next stability step after single-run timing, but no accepted timing result exists yet for these 64x1 and 1x64 filelist-derived shapes.
